ig_caption:
Why is the Golden Gate Bridge orange? Because the steel arrived painted in red primer, and the architect liked it. ⏱️

A pier poured inside a wall in the open ocean, then pumped dry. 227 m towers. Two cables spun from 27,572 wires each. A deck hung outward from both towers.

The Navy wanted black-and-yellow stripes. Irving Morrow kept the primer's warm colour instead: International Orange. 🧡

And a safety net under the deck caught 19 men. They called themselves the Halfway to Hell Club.

Would you have worked 227 m up with only a net below? Yes or no 👇

Next: the Burj Khalifa. Follow so you don't miss it.

yt_description:
A pier built inside a fender wall in the open ocean and pumped dry, 227 m steel towers, main cables spun from 27,572 wires each, and a deck hung outward from both towers (1933–1937). The steel arrived in red-lead primer; architect Irving Morrow turned that colour into International Orange (the Navy had wanted black-and-yellow stripes). A safety net under the deck saved 19 workers, the 'Halfway to Hell Club'.

Sources: https://www.goldengate.org/bridge/history-research/bridge-construction/construction/ · https://www.goldengate.org/bridge/history-research/bridge-features/color-art-deco-styling/ · https://www.history.com/articles/6-things-you-may-not-know-about-the-golden-gate-bridge · https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Gate_Bridge
Figures are historical estimates. Animation is a stylised reconstruction.
